title: Successive internal bar augmentations are quasi-isomorphisms
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on the small coherent profinite site in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $G,H$ be profinite groups. For $P=1,G,H,G\times H$, let $\mathcal A_P(A)$ be the category of internal $A$-modules with an $A$-linear action of the condensed group $\underline P$, with the inflation adjunctions of [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation]. Internal modules are those of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]; write $U_P:\mathcal A_P(A)\to\mathcal A_1(A)$ for forgetting the action, $A[S]$ for the free internal module on a profinite set $S$ [def-sfb-condensed-free-module-adjunction], and $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A$ for the internal module Hom [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed].
Let $N\in\mathcal A_{G\times H}(A)$ and let $N[0]\to I^\bullet$ be a nonnegative injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Use ordinary K-injective derived functors [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and write $Q$ for localization of complexes at quasi-isomorphisms.
Put $C^{a,b,q}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[G^a\times H^b],U_{G\times H}I^q)$ for $a,b,q\geq0$. In each group direction use inhomogeneous bar cofaces (first face acts on the coefficient, interior faces multiply adjacent parameters, final face drops the last parameter) and codegeneracies inserting the identity. Write $D=\operatorname{Tot}_{n,q}C^{n,n,q}$ with differential $\delta_{\rm diag}+(-1)^nd_q$, and $T=\operatorname{Tot}_{a,b,q}C$ with differential $\delta_G+(-1)^a\delta_H+(-1)^{a+b}d_q$; totals have finite sums in each degree [def-sp-double-complex-total].
Set $K^{a,q}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[G^a],(I^q)^H)$ with residual $G$-action on $(I^q)^H$, $L=\operatorname{Tot}_{a,q}K$ with differential $\delta_G+(-1)^ad_q$, and $J^\bullet=(I^\bullet)^{G\times H}$. For fixed $a,q$, the $H$-invariant inclusion makes
$$0\longrightarrow K^{a,q}\longrightarrow C^{a,0,q}\longrightarrow C^{a,1,q}\longrightarrow\cdots$$
an exact augmented complex of internal modules, equivariant for the residual $G$-action. On every profinite $S$, its sections identify with the augmented equivariant Hom complex
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A_H(A)}(A[S]\otimes_AA[G^a]\otimes_AP_{H,\bullet},\operatorname{Res}_H I^q),$$
where $P_{H,b}=A[H^{b+1}]$ has diagonal homogeneous $H$-action, differential the alternating sum of deletions, and augmentation $[h]\mapsto1$; the factor $A[S]\otimes_AA[G^a]$ has trivial $H$-action. The homogeneous-to-inhomogeneous identification includes the action first face. Likewise the $G$ bar of $(I^q)^H$, tested on $S$, has exact augmented section complex $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A_G(A)}(A[S]\otimes_AP_{G,\bullet},(I^q)^H)$, whose augmentation is $J^q=((I^q)^H)^G$ and whose unaugmented terms are $K^{a,q}(S)$.
The invariant inclusions define quasi-isomorphisms $j_K:J^\bullet\to L$ and $k:L\to T$, supported respectively in $a=0$ and $b=0$. Thus they specify isomorphisms
$$Q(J^\bullet)\xrightarrow[Q(j_K)]{\sim}Q(L)\xrightarrow[Q(k)]{\sim}Q(T),\qquad Q(J^\bullet)\cong R\Gamma_G R\Gamma_H^G(N[0]).$$
These are derived-object assertions with the specified augmentations and the ordered total signs above. They include trivial groups and zero modules; no exactness of $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[G^a],-)$ or projectivity of $A[G^a]$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-restriction] to the specified resolution. For each $q$, $\operatorname{Res}_H I^q$ is injective in $\mathcal A_H(A)$ and $(I^q)^H$ is injective in $\mathcal A_G(A)$. The complex $(I^\bullet)^H$ is K-injective in $\mathcal A_G(A)$ and represents $R\Gamma_H^G(N[0])$. These are assertions about this resolution; $(I^\bullet)^H$ need not resolve $N^H[0]$. The action categories are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation], and forgetting action reflects exactness by the restriction lemma.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of successive internal bar augmentations

proof.text:
Fix $a,q$ and a profinite $S$. Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-injective-bar-rows] to the group $H$, the injective $\operatorname{Res}_H I^q$, and the test parameter $S\times G^a$. The free-product tensor isomorphisms of [lem-sfb-condensed-free-linearization-tensor] identify $A[S\times G^a]$ with $A[S]\otimes_A A[G^a]$. The same node identifies maps from a free module with natural assignments on generalized generators and makes its tensor comparison compatible with the underlying-sheaf-preserving equivalence to section-module sheaves. Evaluation on the identity of a representable parameter therefore identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(A[S],M)$ with $M(S)$; transporting the closed adjunction of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] along that equivalence consequently identifies $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[G^a],M)(S)$ with $M(S\times G^a)$. Thus the exact augmented section complex supplied by the bar-row lemma is exactly
$$0\to K^{a,q}(S)\to C^{a,0,q}(S)\to C^{a,1,q}(S)\to\cdots,$$
and its homogeneous description is $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A_H(A)}(A[S]\otimes_A A[G^a]\otimes_A P_{H,\bullet},\operatorname{Res}_H I^q)$, with trivial $H$-action on both parameter factors. The augmentation is the $H$-invariant inclusion. The product $S\times G^a$ remains profinite in the fixed universe, also for $a=0$ or $S=\varnothing$. No exactness of internal Hom is being applied.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of successive internal bar augmentations

proof.text:
The homogeneous formula in [lem-sfb-condensed-injective-bar-rows], with $s$ and the $G^a$ tuple as passive parameters, is
$$f(s,\mathbf g;h_0,\ldots,h_b)=h_0c(s,\mathbf g;h_0^{-1}h_1,\ldots,h_{b-1}^{-1}h_b).$$
It gives precisely the action first face, adjacent multiplication faces, last deletion face and identity-inserting codegeneracies required in the statement. All these formulas commute with restrictions of test sets. The residual $G$-action is coefficientwise: for every generalized $u\in\underline G(V)$, the product action gives $u(h_0c)=h_0(uc)$. Hence the displayed identification, differential and augmentation are $G$-equivariant. Exactness on every section, proved in step 2, gives equality of image and kernel sheaves: every kernel section already has a preimage over the same test set. Forgetting action reflects exactness by [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-restriction], so the augmented $H$ complex is also exact with residual action. Finally $\delta_G$, $\delta_H$ and $d_q$ commute: parameter pullbacks in different directions commute, their first faces commute because the two coefficient actions commute, and $d_q$ is equivariant. This also proves compatibility of the augmentations with the $G$ and resolution differentials.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of successive internal bar augmentations

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-injective-bar-rows] again, now to $G$, the injective $(I^q)^H$ of step 1, and the arbitrary test set $S$. It gives the exact augmented section complex
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A_G(A)}(A[S]\otimes_A P_{G,\bullet},(I^q)^H),$$
whose unaugmented terms are $K^{a,q}(S)$ and whose initial term is $((I^q)^H)^G(S)$. By [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation], the last invariant module is $J^q$ by the identity on the common submodule of $I^q$, including its inclusion. The bar-row lemma gives the stipulated faces and degeneracies and compatibility with equivariant coefficient maps, hence with $d_q$. Thus the row augmentation is exactly the degree-zero inclusion used to define $j_K$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of successive internal bar augmentations

proof.text: For the first-quadrant double complex $K^{a,q}$, the inclusions $J^q\to K^{0,q}$ form a chain map in $q$ and are killed by the next $G$ differential. By step 4 each map from $J^q$ concentrated in bar degree zero into $K^{\bullet,q}$ induces an isomorphism on every cohomology object. Apply [lem-sc-first-quadrant-column-augmentation], with its first index equal to $a$ and second index equal to $q$. Its actual augmentation into the finite-diagonal total is $j_K$, and its total differential is $\delta_G+(-1)^a d_q$ by [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Therefore $j_K:J^\bullet\to L$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0133, lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution, variant interchanging the two variables; apply to the exact augmented G rows

proof.text:
To totalize the $H$ augmentation, put
$$E^{b,r}=\bigoplus_{a+q=r}C^{a,b,q},\qquad d_b=\delta_H,\qquad d_r=\delta_G+(-1)^a d_q.$$
Step 3 shows that these are commuting differentials and that $d_r^2=0$ (the two cross terms have opposite signs). This is first-quadrant. For fixed $r$, the augmentation from $L^r=\bigoplus_{a+q=r}K^{a,q}$ into $E^{0,r}$ is an exact augmented $b$ row by step 2: on each test set a kernel tuple has one preimage in each of the finitely many summands, and these preimages give a preimage tuple. The augmentation commutes with $d_r$ by step 3, and $d_b$ kills it. Apply [lem-sc-first-quadrant-column-augmentation] with indices $(b,r)$. It gives a quasi-isomorphism $\widetilde k:L\to\operatorname{Tot}_{b,r}E$ supported in $b=0$. The differential of this total, on $C^{a,b,q}$, is
$$\delta_H+(-1)^b\delta_G+(-1)^{a+b}d_q.$$
Only finitely many summands occur in each degree.

source.place: Tag 0133, lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution, second-variable variant, applied after grouping the finite (a,q) diagonals

proof.text: Reassociate the finite sums and multiply the $C^{a,b,q}$ summand by $(-1)^{ab}$. This defines a cochain isomorphism $s:\operatorname{Tot}_{b,r}E\to T$: the coefficients of $s\,d$ in the $G$, $H$, and $q$ directions are respectively $(-1)^{b+(a+1)b}=(-1)^{ab}$, $(-1)^{a(b+1)}=(-1)^{ab+a}$, and $(-1)^{ab+a+b}$, exactly those of $d_Ts$. The inverse uses the same signs. On $b=0$ this sign is $1$, so $s\widetilde k$ is the specified invariant inclusion $k:L\to T$, without any extra augmentation sign. It is a quasi-isomorphism because $s$ is a cochain isomorphism and $\widetilde k$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of successive internal bar augmentations

proof.text: Localizing the two quasi-isomorphisms gives the two displayed isomorphisms with arrows $Q(j_K)$ and $Q(k)$ by [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. To identify their common source, use [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-restriction]: $(I^\bullet)^H$ is already a K-injective representative of $R\Gamma_H^G(N[0])$ in $D(\mathcal A_G(A))$. Therefore the ordinary right-derived-functor computation on a K-injective, as specified in [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], computes $R\Gamma_G R\Gamma_H^G(N[0])$ by $Q(((I^\bullet)^H)^G)$. The identity of invariants in [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation] identifies this complex with $J^\bullet$, including its maps. This proves the derived-object assertion, rather than merely cohomology comparisons. All row lemmas permit trivial groups and zero coefficients. For a trivial group the unnormalized bar still has positive terms, with successive differentials $0,1,0,1,\ldots$ and degree-zero identity augmentation; the same comparisons apply. For $N=0$ every chosen nonnegative injective resolution still satisfies step 1. None of the steps requires $A[G^a]$ to be projective or its internal Hom functor to be exact.
